solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fish grabbing snail in the middle, cracking shell (8)

indicators.note: the fish takes hold of the letter, so it goes inside
points to the central letter of snail

blocks.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
the centre letter of snAil, placed inside CARP

annotation.surface: A fish seizes a snail and breaks open its shell to eat it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking shell' reads as one action, but cracking is an adjective meaning excellent, and shell alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a tortoise, crab or similar animal.

entries.clue: Heinous violent assault — officer’s jacket torn apart (9)

indicators.note: a jacket is the outside layer, so take the outer letters of officer

blocks.note: ABH = actual bodily harm, a British criminal charge for violent assault
rent = torn apart, as in a garment rent in two

annotation.surface: A brutal attack in which an officer's jacket was ripped to shreds.
annotation.walkthrough: ABH (actual bodily harm) is the British legal term for a serious assault, just short of GBH (grievous bodily harm).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe conduct so wicked it provokes loathing.

entries.clue: Bogart is terribly engaging performer (7)

indicators.note: the phrase engages, or holds, the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Bogart, through is, into the start of terribly

annotation.surface: A tribute to Humphrey Bogart as a wonderfully charming screen actor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly engaging' reads as praise, but 'terribly' only supplies letters and 'engaging' is the instruction; Bogart is fittingly an artiste himself.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from French, used especially of music-hall and cabaret entertainers.

entries.clue: Character I will follow? (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants a person or personality; the setter means a letter of the alphabet
the surface wants a vow of loyalty; the setter means the letter I comes next in the alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone vowing to be a follower of a strong personality.
annotation.walkthrough: Character here is a letter of the alphabet: I comes straight after H, so H is the character I will follow. AITCH is how the letter H is spelt out.
annotation.definitionFit: AITCH is the name of the letter H, which the letter I follows in the alphabet.

entries.clue: Runner departs from place of work (3)

indicators.note: D (departs, as in timetables) leaves the word

blocks.note: a desk is where you work
d = departs, taken away from DESK

annotation.surface: A jogger heads out from the office.
annotation.walkthrough: A runner in crosswords is often a river; the Esk is a river in Scotland and northern England.
annotation.definitionFit: The Esk is a river, and a river runs.

entries.clue: Revolutionary group involved in covering up minor attack (6)

indicators.note: revolving turns the letters round
the group of letters is caught up inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of covering, all of up and the start of minor
surface padding: the group is simply the run of letters caught up in the phrase

annotation.surface: A band of rebels is caught hushing up a small-scale raid.
annotation.walkthrough: The group is just a group of letters, not a band of revolutionaries: read coveriNG UP MInor backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: To impugn is to attack as false or wrong, usually someone's motives or honesty.

entries.clue: Copying Ipswich’s first change, one’s substituted for United (9)

indicators.note: take the opening letter of Ipswich
I takes the place of U in the word

blocks.note: change = MUTATION, with I (one) put in place of U (United)

annotation.surface: Ipswich Town's opening substitution, one player coming on in place of a Manchester United man.
annotation.walkthrough: U for United is standard in football results, and I is the Roman numeral one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: copying someone's manner or work is the same as imitating it.

entries.clue: Stewed dish I’d mentioned (3-4)

indicators.note: said out loud, so a sound-alike

annotation.surface: Someone recalls suggesting a stew for dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: Stewed looks like a cooking word next to dish, but it is slang for drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Pie-eyed and stewed are both slang for drunk.

entries.clue: Supporting line’s wrapped around stone in such conditions (5)

annotation.definition: Supporting line’s wrapped around stone in such conditions

indicators.note: the guy goes round the stone, holding it inside

blocks.note: a guy is a rope holding up a tent
st = stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

annotation.surface: Tent guy ropes weighted down with stones because of the weather.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: guys are tied round stones to hold a tent down precisely when it is windy.
annotation.definitionFit: Gusty weather, with strong bursts of wind, is when tent lines need anchoring with stones.

entries.clue: Slug ruined photograph (4)

blocks.note: a third definition, the informal sense of worn out or broken beyond repair

annotation.surface: A garden pest has spoilt a picture.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: a slug is a shot of spirits (or a bullet), shot means ruined, and a shot is a photograph. The garden pest is a red herring.
annotation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a measure of spirits (a slug), a bullet (also a slug), and a snapped picture.

entries.clue: New Ikea seat becoming centrepiece of trendy lounge (4,2,4)

indicators.note: a new arrangement of the letters
the jumble goes in the middle of what follows

blocks.note: the outer letters of TrendY, wrapped around the anagram

annotation.surface: A new flat-pack chair takes pride of place in a fashionable living room.
annotation.walkthrough: Lounge looks like the room the seat is in, but it is a verb, and only trendy's outside letters are used, with the anagram as its centrepiece.
annotation.definitionFit: Lounge as a verb means to loaf about idly, which the phrase says in three words.

entries.clue: Cold butter has torn bread (10)

indicators.note: ripped up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: c = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Butter straight from the fridge rips the bread when you try to spread it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a real kitchen annoyance: cold butter does tear bread.
annotation.definitionFit: Bruschetta is Italian toasted bread, usually rubbed with garlic and topped.

entries.clue: Obsolete fuel might ultimately have decline reversed (4,3)

indicators.note: take the final letter of might
the word for decline is turned round

blocks.note: sag = decline; turned round it gives GAS

annotation.surface: An old fuel whose falling use might in the end be turned around.
annotation.walkthrough: Might and have look like verbs in one sentence, but might gives only its last letter and have is OWN.
annotation.definitionFit: Town gas, made from coal and piped to homes, was replaced by natural gas.

entries.clue: Scratching head, son repeatedly twisted plaything (2-2)

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter
something done repeatedly happens more than once, so the headless son appears twice in a row
turned round, reversing the letters

blocks.note: son = BOY, twice, each losing its head B: OY OY, then turned round

annotation.surface: A puzzled child keeps twisting a toy round and round.
annotation.walkthrough: Scratching head looks like a puzzled gesture, but it tells you to scratch out the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a toy spun up and down on a string.

entries.clue: Female always starts to feel energised with medicinal herb (8)

indicators.note: take the opening letters of the next three words

blocks.note: the first letters of Feel Energised With

annotation.surface: A woman who always feels perked up after taking a herbal remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a herbal-remedy testimonial, and the answer is exactly such a remedy.
annotation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like herb traditionally used against fevers and migraines.

entries.clue: One’s extremely lucky with tiny cut during boxing match? (9)

indicators.note: take the extreme letters of lucky
a word that is cut is shortened, here by losing its final letter
these letters go in the middle of the fight

blocks.note: a fight; opened after F to take the rest

annotation.surface: A boxer got lucky that only a small cut opened during the bout.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'One', meaning one of the boxers, and the question mark flags that a fight with a boxer in it is a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A flyweight is a boxer in one of the lightest weight classes, so one who might be in a boxing match.

entries.clue: Colour’s popular, regularly adding “wow” (6)

indicators.note: take every other letter of adding

annotation.surface: A shade that has become fashionable keeps getting admired.
annotation.walkthrough: Adding looks like the join between popular and wow, but it supplies letters of its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet colour.

entries.clue: Hound’s eager and playful, nipping cat’s tail (5,4)

indicators.note: the letters play about, so rearrange them
an animal's tail is its hindmost part, so the last letter of cat
the letters take in that T as they are mixed

blocks.note: the last letter of caT, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A frisky dog snaps at a cat's tail.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture of a dog chasing a cat is entirely apt, and the answer is exactly such a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: A Great Dane is a very large breed of dog.

entries.clue: Well-built enclosure receiving go-ahead to accommodate 100 (6)

indicators.note: the enclosure takes the go-ahead inside it
the go-ahead in turn holds the 100

blocks.note: a sty is a pig's pen

annotation.surface: A solidly built pen gets approval to house a hundred animals.
annotation.walkthrough: Well-built reads as describing the enclosure but it is the definition, of a person.
annotation.definitionFit: Stocky means sturdily built, broad and solid.

entries.clue: Church in its current condition retains steeple’s initial frame (7)

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letter inside it
the first letter of steeple

blocks.note: as is = unchanged, in its present state
the first letter of Steeple, held inside AS IS

annotation.surface: A church, left unrestored, still has the original framework of its spire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In its current condition' is a longhand way of saying AS IS, as in sold as is.
annotation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a vehicle or other construction.

entries.clue: Worry about turning against Glasgow’s foremost criminal (8)

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the word for about is written backwards
the foremost part of a word is its first letter
against in the sense of up against, touching, so G sits right beside ANGST

blocks.note: re = about; turned round it gives ER

annotation.surface: Concern about Glasgow's leading crook changing sides.
annotation.walkthrough: Worry wants to be NAG with 'about turning' reversing it; the worry is ANGST, and only 'about' turns.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a gangster is one particular kind of criminal, the violent gang member.

entries.clue: Iron shed left attached to rear of house (7)

indicators.note: the rear of a house is its back end, so its last letter
joined on, so the pieces simply follow one another

annotation.surface: An iron garden shed bolted on to the back of a house.
annotation.walkthrough: Iron reads as the shed's building material, but it is the definition: irons are fetters.
annotation.definitionFit: Irons are chains for a prisoner, and one such iron is a shackle.

entries.clue: Seabirds rejected one from another species? (4)

indicators.note: sent back, so the word is reversed

annotation.surface: Seabirds shunning a newcomer from a different species.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a seabird, but not an auk, hence 'another species' with a question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A skua is a predatory seabird, a different species from the auks it is spelt from.

entries.clue: Tokyo — busy city (5)

indicators.note: the letters are bustling about, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: A description of Tokyo as a bustling metropolis.
annotation.walkthrough: Kyoto is Tokyo rearranged, and fittingly was Japan's capital before Tokyo.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Kyoto, the old imperial capital of Japan, is one city among many.

entries.clue: Something added to bath soap smelt funny — sulphur? (5,5)

indicators.note: odd, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

annotation.surface: A bather notices the soap smells odd, perhaps of sulphur.
annotation.walkthrough: Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate, so the sulphur in the surface is actually in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are dissolved in bathwater to soothe aching muscles.

entries.clue: Originally misunderstanding etiquette, picked up wine (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of misunderstanding
lifted, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

blocks.note: a code of conduct; read upwards it gives EDOC

annotation.surface: A guest who got the dinner manners wrong has taken up the wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Picked up reads as lifting a glass, but in a down clue it turns CODE upside down.
annotation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

entries.clue: Rescuers firm as wind from the east loses strength, finally (10)

indicators.note: read from right to left, so reversed
whatever a word loses is taken out of it, here one letter
the letter lost is the last of strength

blocks.note: a draught of air, losing H to give DRAUGT
the last letter of strengtH, removed

annotation.surface: A sea rescue team holds firm as an easterly gale dies down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loses strength' sounds like the wind dropping, but with 'finally' it means losing only the last letter of strength.
annotation.definitionFit: The coastguard is the service that rescues people in trouble at sea.

entries.clue: Program’s content lacking boundaries (3)

indicators.note: the word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: content in the adjective sense, satisfied; its first and last letters go

annotation.surface: Software whose contents have no limits.
annotation.walkthrough: Content looks like the noun (what's in the program), but it is the adjective, happy.
annotation.definitionFit: An app is a software program, especially for a phone.

entries.clue: King Henry meets an Eastern ruler (4)

indicators.note: things that meet come together, so the pieces are joined end to end

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Henry VIII has a summit with a monarch from Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: King Henry reads as one Tudor monarch, but it splits into K and H; the henry is the unit of electrical inductance.
annotation.definitionFit: A khan is a ruler or chief in Central Asia, as in Genghis Khan.

entries.clue: Garment’s stiff — pressure’s released by assistant at the back (6)

indicators.note: the P is let go from the word
the last letter of assistant

blocks.note: a stiff is a corpse, losing P to give CORSE

annotation.surface: A rigid undergarment is loosened by a helper standing behind the wearer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is someone being unlaced from behind, but stiff is slang for a dead body.
annotation.definitionFit: A corset is a close-fitting, stiffened undergarment.

entries.clue: Fish before on best lake (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after

blocks.note: the pick of the bunch = the best

annotation.surface: Fish is served ahead of the finest lake produce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' reads as placement, but it gives ERE, and 'on' does the placing.
annotation.definitionFit: A pickerel is a small pike, a freshwater fish.
